os-error-text: When the exe cannot be verified the TS warns "could not be verified (<String(error)>)" with Node's text, for example `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '<path>'`. A Rust io::Error prints differently (`No such file or directory (os error 2)`), so the replay compares each warning up to and including 'could not be verified (' and requires the error name ENOENT to be mapped to the platform's not-found text; every other warning and every info line is compared byte for byte.
wrong-case-spelling-is-not-recorded: A wrong-case spelling of an existing file (BIN/GAME.EXE for bin/game.exe) is accepted on a case-insensitive volume and rejected on a case-sensitive one, so no golden holds it. mixed-case-path-with-the-exact-spelling holds a tree whose file is really spelled Data/Game.EXE and asks for exactly that.
info-line-names-the-relative-override: The TS info line is `known-fix launchArgs [...], exeOverride <the resolved absolute path>`; the Rust line names the override as the fix file spells it (`exeOverride bin/game.exe`). EngineLog rule (gamelib-engine sinks.rs): no absolute path in gamelib.log. It is a log-text difference only: the answer still carries the resolved path. Affected case: knownFixLaunch--readknownfixlaunchoverrides-returns-launchargs-and-a-resolved-exeoverride. The replay (golden_launch_overrides.rs expected_line) rewrites the golden's absolute path to its install-relative form and refuses a path outside the install.
